title: Fallback Patterns
description: Learn fallback patterns to provide graceful degradation when services fail.

data.text: Fallback patterns provide alternative behavior when a primary operation fails. Netflix uses fallbacks extensively—when recommendations fail, they show popular content; when search fails, they show categories. Fallbacks ensure users always get a response, even during failures.

data.title: Common Fallback Approaches
items: Static fallback: Return cached or default data
Alternative service: Call a secondary service or API
Queue for later: Store request for async processing
User notification: Inform user of issue and suggest alternative

data.text: Fallbacks are typically implemented alongside circuit breakers. When the circuit is open or a call fails, the fallback logic executes. Fallbacks should be fast, safe, and provide a reasonable user experience.

data.title: Netflix Fallback Example
data.text: Netflix's recommendation service uses a fallback to popular content when the primary algorithm fails. Users still see content, just not personalized recommendations.

data.title: Example: Fallback with Circuit Breaker
data.code: Implement a fallback when the recommendation service fails.

data.caption: Fallback pattern flow
data.definition:
graph LR
    C[Client] --> P[Primary Service]
    P -->|Success| R[Response]
    P -->|Failure| FB[Fallback]
    FB -->|Cached/Degraded| R

items.question: What makes a good fallback?
items.answer: A good fallback is fast, safe, and provides acceptable user experience. It should not call other unreliable services or perform complex operations.

items.question: Should I show the user a degraded experience?
items.answer: Yes, but be transparent. Show a message like 'Showing popular content because recommendations are temporarily unavailable.' This manages expectations.

items.question: Can fallbacks cause data inconsistencies?
items.answer: Yes, if the fallback writes data differently. Ensure fallbacks do not create duplicate or inconsistent data. Prefer read-only fallbacks when possible.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Fallbacks provide graceful degradation during failures
Use cached or default data when possible
Be transparent with users about degraded experiences
data.takeaway: Fallbacks ensure users always get a response, maintaining trust even during failures.
